- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing immediate price momentum.
- After a spike (e.g., 38+), model often overshoots in the immediate aftermath, then corrects — indicating overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Model shows weak mean reversion: fails to anticipate sharp reversals or corrections after high peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, missing late-stage price surges (e.g., 40+).
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-stage price increases, especially after 30–40 days of history.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture abrupt, non-linear price jumps or sudden drops.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values, especially when recent history includes high prices — underestimates the “carryover” effect of recent spikes.
